{"name": "charge-review", "steps": "Inputs: the developer's org or account id, the invoice (id or month), the lines and amounts they mean, request ids if they have them.

1. Identify the account. If you have neither org nor account id, ask_developer for org_id (plus invoice_id/invoice_month and line_items/amounts/request_ids in the same call if not given). lookup_account.
2. Check billing channel, plan and has_signed_contract on the account.
   - Not billed directly by Redwood: search_knowledge for the procedure for that exact channel (cloud marketplace vs reseller are different pages; apply only the one matching billing_channel). Support credits/disputes nothing there; tell the developer who bills them and where refunds/credits/invoices go. Open a case only if the current page says so (e.g. a metering mismatch).
3. get_invoice (map a month to an id from lookup_account's invoice list). Read console_confirmed_duplicates (original_line vs copy_lines, decided by where the usage records point), same_requests_but_unconfirmed, and same_amount_but_different_requests. get_usage for request ids the developer gave.
4. Classify:
   a. Console-confirmed duplicate: act only on the copy line, never the original.
   b. Look-alike (same amount/description, different request ids), no second line, or usage pointing to neither/both lines: NOT a confirmed duplicate. Say so plainly with the console evidence. Never say a credit is likely before the console confirms a duplicate.
   c. Wrong rate/quantity/product, unrecognized usage, retries/cancelled streams, token mismatch: search the usage/token pages; if they explain it, explain and stop.
   d. Waive/reduce a correct charge (goodwill, exception, SLA credit, refund): not Support's to issue. Load team-handoff.
5. For (a), search_knowledge for what Support may do now: the Support charter (which accounts Support may credit at all), the credits-and-disputes page, and Finance's approval matrix for the per-line limit. The limit can depend on how the invoice was rated (e.g. which price book applies to the invoice's usage period): search the Finance close calendar for that, using the invoice period. Drafts, proposals and threads change nothing.
   - Support may credit this account and the copy line's full amount is within the limit: confirm_with_developer "I'll issue a credit note of $X (full amount) on the duplicated line L of invoice I." Only after yes: issue_credit_note (reason duplicate, memo with request ids). Tell them the credit note id and amount, and when it applies if the page says. No handoff.
   - Over the limit, or an account Support may not credit (e.g. contract/enterprise per the charter): do not credit or split. confirm_with_developer "I'll open a dispute on line L of invoice I (duplicate charge, request ids R) and hand it to Billing Ops." After yes: open_dispute, then load team-handoff and escalate with the dispute id.
   - If the developer says no: write nothing (no credit, dispute or case); say nothing was changed and they can come back.
6. For (b) and unexplained (c): gather intake (invoice, both lines, window in the account's billing timezone, request ids, what they checked) with ask_developer, then load team-handoff.
7. Never promise a dispute outcome or date. If a write is rejected, read get_invoice to see the state before saying anything."}

body: ## Purpose
The support console can look up a customer's billing account, issue a credit note against invoice lines, and open a billing dispute. This page defines when Support uses each one. It amends the billing routing page for duplicate charges only; everything else on that page still applies. This version is effective from 26 February 2027 and adds how to tell the copy from the original. Support's per-line limit is set in Finance's Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix (Finance shared drive), which FP&A revised in February 2027; check the matrix for the limit that applies to the invoice in front of you."}, {"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/billing-adjustments-approval-matrix.json", "chunk": "5/7", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix", "status": "final", "date": "2027-02-26", "text": "## Evidence each adjustment needs
- **Duplicate-charge credit**: the invoice number, both line IDs and the request IDs they bill. The console confirms the duplicate; a matching description or amount alone is not evidence.
- **Billing-error correction**: the line, the expected rate or quantity and where it comes from (price book, order form).
- **Goodwill and SLA credits**: the customer's ask, the amount if given, and the reason. The account team adds contract references for SLA claims.
- **Write-offs**: collections history and the Controller's note."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-duplicate-charges-and-disputes-2027.json", "chunk": "6/7", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes (v2)", "status": "published", "date": "2027-02-26", "text": "## What Billing Ops needs in a duplicate handoff
| Field | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| Invoice number | The console invoice record |
| Both line IDs, original and copy | The console invoice lines |
| Request IDs | The customer, checked against the usage records |
| Window | In the account's billing timezone |
| Dispute id | The dispute you opened, when the line is over the limit |
| What the customer asked for | The conversation |
## After a credit note
- The credit is applied to the next invoice, or to the invoice being issued if it is issued before the close (see Finance's close calendar).
- The customer sees it as a credit line with the original invoice number.
- Don't issue a second credit note for the same line. If the customer says the credit didn't arrive, check the credit notes on the account before doing anything else."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/duplicate-charges-and-refunds-help-2025.json", "chunk": "1/1", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Help Center: Duplicate Charges and Refunds (archived)", "status": "published ARCHIVED", "date": "2026-01-21", "text": "title: Help Center: Duplicate Charges and Refunds (archived)

body: > Archived 2026-01-21. This help-center article is no longer current. Support handles duplicate charges as described on "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes".
## Duplicate charges
If your invoice bills the same usage twice, contact Support with the invoice number. Support refunds a duplicated line in full on request.
## Refund timing
Refunds reach your card within 5-10 business days."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-billing-credits-and-disputes.json", "chunk": "3/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes", "status": "published SUPERSEDED by 'Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes (v2)' effective 2027-02-26", "date": "2026-02-05", "text": "(continued) ## Duplicate charges: what Support may credit
| Situation | What Support does |
|---|---|
| Confirmed duplicate, duplicated line over the limit | Don't credit. Open a dispute on the duplicated line (reason `duplicate_charge`, with the request IDs) and hand the case to Billing Ops with the invoice number, the line and the dispute id. |
| Duplicate the console doesn't confirm (different request IDs, or no second line) | Don't credit. Collect the intake details and hand the case to Billing Ops as the routing page describes. |
Support's limit is set by Finance in the Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix (Finance shared drive) (the duplicate-charge credit row). It is per duplicated line and applies to the line's full amount. Don't split a larger duplicate into several smaller credits."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-billing-credits-and-disputes.json", "chunk": "2/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes", "status": "published SUPERSEDED by 'Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes (v2)' effective 2027-02-26", "date": "2026-02-05", "text": "## Look up the account first
- Look up the customer's billing account in the console before you quote an amount, a plan, an invoice line, or whether a charge is a duplicate. You can find the account by its account id or by the customer's org name; ask for one of them if the customer hasn't given either.
- Quote amounts as the console shows them. Don't restate a figure the customer gives you as fact.
## Duplicate charges: what Support may credit
A charge is a confirmed duplicate only when the console shows two lines on the same direct Redwood invoice that bill the same request IDs. A similar description or the same amount on its own is not enough.
| Situation | What Support does |
|---|---|
| Confirmed duplicate, duplicated line within Support's limit | Issue one credit note with reason `duplicate` for the full amount of the duplicated line, against that line. No handoff is needed. Tell the customer the amount credited. |"}]}

FP&A reviews the limits each quarter against adjustment volume and error rates. Changes are announced in #support and #billing-ops and logged below. A limit change applies from the date or period stated in the log; earlier adjustments keep the limit in force when they were issued.

| 2025-09-08 | First version | Rishi Malhotra |"}, {"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/billing-adjustments-approval-matrix.json", "chunk": "2/7", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix", "status": "final", "date": "2027-02-26", "text": "## Scope
- Direct Redwood invoices for Hosted API, Embeddings, Batch and Dedicated.
- Marketplace purchases are out of scope: adjustments go through the marketplace (see the marketplace invoicing notes).
- Contracted Enterprise accounts follow this matrix unless their order form names a different approver.
## Definitions
- **Adjustment**: any change to what a customer owes after an invoice is issued: a credit note, a refund, a write-off or a re-issued invoice.
- **Per line**: the amount of one invoice line, taken whole. An adjustment is never split across several smaller ones to stay under a limit.
- **Billing error**: a line that bills the wrong rate, quantity or product, or bills the same usage twice.
- **Goodwill**: any reduction of a correct charge, for any reason."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-duplicate-charges-and-disputes-2027.json", "chunk": "1/7", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes (v2)", "status": "published", "date": "2027-02-26", "text": "title: Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes (v2)

body: ## Scope
Credit memos that Partnerships raises through the AWS or GCP marketplace for marketplace-billed customers. They are not Support console credit notes, and they don't apply to direct Redwood invoices; Support's own limit is in the Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix.
## Limits
- Up to $1,000 per memo: Partnerships.
- Above $1,000: FP&A.

{"query": "2027 Finance Close Calendar which price book applies to March 2027 usage invoice periods", "results": [{"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/2027-close-calendar-and-invoice-periods.json", "chunk": "3/4", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods", "status": "final", "date": "2027-02-22", "text": "## Late usage

A price-book change applies to usage from the first period that starts on or after its effective date. Mid-period changes are not prorated unless the order form says so.

{"name": "team-handoff", "steps": "1. Decide whether a case is needed at all. search_knowledge for the routing policy covering this request (e.g. "billing case routing <topic>", "who approves <request>"). 2. Pick the owning team from the current routing/approval/charter documents, not from drafts, proposals or chat threads. Use the console account (plan, channel, contracts) to choose between rows, e.g. self-serve vs signed contract, direct vs marketplace. Collect the intake the receiving team needs (the routing page lists it per row) with one ask_developer call: e.g. invoice_id, line_items, amounts, request_ids, time_of_issue together with timezone, error_code, checks_done, contract. 5. escalate_case with: team; priority as the current pages say (normal for billing handoffs unless the routing page says urgent); summary (what they asked, what the console shows, what the team must decide/do); details with every fact given (ids, amounts as the console shows them, window in billing timezone, request ids, amount requested if any, what's missing); dispute_id if any.
